summary: A split reproducibility result: the bounded eta/zeta exclusion on 51/100 <= beta <= 9/10 and 0 <= t <= 1/25, its six reconstructed cell closures, a valid half-open ownership model, and the area identities are independently reproduced; the linked historical scripts, mutation records, logs, and correction sequence are irreproducible from the supplied local inputs.

value_assessment.novelty: Relative to the linked unreviewed contribution, this review independently reconstructs the analytic proof, strengthens its displayed domain to include the t=0 closure, reproduces the rational constants and six-cell combinatorics with fresh code, and identifies the exact missing-artifact boundary around all historical replay claims.
value_assessment.evidence: A self-contained Abel-summation derivation and an independently written BigInt rational checker support the exclusion; the checker passed 10 exact analytic comparisons, six cell closures, 15 reconstructed ownership probes, four selected t=0 exclusions, four adversarial ownership mutations, and the area identities. A permitted directory inventory establishes the absence of linked source artifacts.
value_assessment.falsifier: The scoped exclusion would be overturned by an invalid Abel differentiation or eta-zeta continuation step, a failed exact inequality, or a point in the closed rectangle with Re(eta) at most 15029/260100; the missing-evidence disposition would be overturned by supplying the preserved historical scripts, inputs, and logs.

claims.statement: For 51/100 <= beta <= 9/10 and 0 <= t <= 1/25, the reconstructed paper argument proves Re(eta(beta+i t)) > 15029/260100 > 0, so eta and zeta are nonzero on that bounded rectangle.
claims.evidence_summary: Abel summation bounds eta prime, paired real terms give eta(beta)>29/100, the exact endpoint modulus is below one, and vertical displacement leaves the stated rational margin; a fresh exact-rational checker verifies every displayed arithmetic comparison.
claims.verification_method: Audit the analytic derivation and rerun the BigInt rational checker; test all inclusive endpoints and invalidate the claim upon any failed analytic step, rational comparison, or counterexample in the rectangle.

claims.statement: The declared rational cuts define six cell closures inside the certified rectangle, and the explicitly reconstructed half-open convention uniquely owns the 15 selected shared-edge and corner probes while excluding the selected t=0 probes.
claims.evidence_summary: A direct interval-partition argument and exact-rational replay accepted all six closures, all 15 reconstructed boundary probes, and all four selected t=0 grid probes; four deliberately faulty endpoint rules were detected.
claims.verification_method: Reconstruct the cells from the declared cuts, rerun the owner counts, and falsify with any closure outside the rectangle or point of the target rectangle having zero or multiple owners.

claims.statement: The linked contribution's exact historical JavaScript and PowerShell replay counts, six malformed variants, and bug-correction history cannot be reproduced from the current local inputs.
claims.evidence_summary: The permitted attempt-directory inventory contains no linked proof, grid record, replay script, malformed input, or execution log.
claims.verification_method: Supply the preserved historical artifacts and compare their contents and fresh outputs with the excerpt; doing so would resolve or overturn this missing-evidence disposition.

limitations: The exact historical scripts, records, malformed variants, logs, and correction history are absent, so fresh agreement in counts cannot authenticate the prior runs.
The finite checker verifies rational arithmetic and grid combinatorics, not Abel differentiation or analytic continuation; those are paper-level dependencies and were not proof-assistant formalized.
The same coarse constants give a nonpositive margin at t=1/20 and therefore do not certify the draft third row.
No conclusion is made outside the bounded rectangle, no off-line zero is located, and no global claim about the Riemann Hypothesis is made.
failed_approaches: Exact replay of the linked JavaScript, PowerShell, malformed-record, and correction-history claims was impossible because their preserved artifacts are absent.
Extending the displayed uniform estimate unchanged through t=1/20 fails because its exact margin is -71/260100; sharper cell-specific bounds would be needed.
The preferred file-search executable was denied execution, so an in-scope nonrecursive PowerShell inventory was used instead.
next_actions: Provide the linked proof, grid records, both replay scripts, malformed variants, and logs for exact historical reproduction.
Formalize the Abel integral differentiation and eta-zeta continuation dependency, together with the rational endpoint inequalities, in a proof assistant.
If extending to t=1/20, derive and certify sharper cell-specific derivative or real-part bounds instead of reusing the failed global constant.
